explanation: Unfused: kernel 1 reads 4 bytes and writes 4 per element, kernel 2 does the same: 16 bytes per element. Fused: 8 bytes. Same bandwidth, half the bytes, twice as fast. Each extra elementwise op in an unfused chain adds 8 more bytes per element, which is why compilers (`torch.compile`, XLA) and hand-written kernels fuse norms, activations, residual adds and dropout into their neighbours.
